name: ask_question
description:
Ask the user a question with the answers written out for them.

One to four questions with choices, or one free-text question with options: [].
A linked task is blocked atomically; omitted task_id uses your active task.
You may continue unrelated work. Collect answers with check_answer, then
explicitly resume the blocked task after its blocker has been resolved.

about.description: `criteria` for a story's acceptance criteria or spec: it goes to product.

questions.description: 1-4 objects: question (required), options (required, [{label, description}]), header, multiSelect.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

task_id.description: Task to block; omitted defaults to your active task.

to.description: `product` for criteria and spec, `main` for everything else (the default). Either answers, hands it to the other, or takes it to the user.

name: assign_subagent
description:
Assign a registered sub-agent to an open task (Story 704 / Rule 4).

Atomically updates `Task.agent_id`: if the sub-agent currently owns a
different task on this session, that task's `agent_id` is cleared and
the target task's `agent_id` is set in the **same** `Repo.update` —
no partial-failure window where the sub-agent ends up unassigned
from their old task while not landing on the new one.

`agent_id` is the Task tool's own result from spawning that sub-agent,
not something to go look up — 50ddc827: `list_session_subagents` (the
tool that *would* answer "who is registered") is not every role's to
call, and the id is already yours from the spawn, every time.

Errors when:
- the `agent_id` is not currently active in `session.subagents`
  (filtered through `Session.active_subagents/2`, so TTL-expired
  registrations are rejected the same way a fully unknown id is)
- the `task_id` is not on the session

agent_id.description: The sub-agent's id, from the Task tool's own result when you spawned it — not something to look up elsewhere

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

name: assign_task
description:
Assign an existing task to a subagent.

The main agent uses this to claim a task on behalf of a subagent
before spawning it. Pass the `agent_id` that the subagent will use
so it appears on the task record immediately.

Returns the work prompt so the main agent can forward it to the subagent.

agent_id.description: Subagent identifier to assign to the task

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

task_id.description: ID of the task to assign

name: cancel_task
description:
Cancel a task on the current session (Story 704 / Rule 4).

Transitions the task to `:cancelled` without going through
`evaluate_task`. Used to unstick the loop when a task can't make
progress and the agent wants to move on. No PermissionSocket
involvement — routine admin owned by the agent.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

name: check_answer
description:
Fetch the reply to a question raised by `ask_user`.

The other half of a deliberately two-step exchange. `ask_user` delivers the
question and returns; this collects the answer whenever the agent gets round
to asking for it.

It waits briefly for an answer event — long enough that a user looking at the question
answers within one call, short enough that the MCP transport never times out.
Answering takes as long as it takes, so `pending` is an ordinary result rather
than a failure: stop, let the stop hook bring you back, and check again.

## Why this no longer goes over HTTP

The same reason `ask_user` stopped, in its own words: this runs *in* the cloud
app, in the same process as `Notifications` and against the same database, so
the request left the VM and came back to call the function that was already in
scope.

Story 896 moved `ask_user` and added `list_user_questions` in-process, and left
this one on `QuestionClient` — so the half of the exchange that *collects* the
answer was the half no spex could drive, and the only untested step in a flow
built to be tested. They were verified to reach the same database, so nothing
was broken; it was a round trip and a blind spot rather than a split brain.

`QuestionClient` is gone entirely — 3b038c842 removed it with the rest of the
arbitrage path. This paragraph said it "stays for the CLI", which was true when
written and outlived the module by two days.

name: evaluate_task
description:
Evaluate a task's work and get pass/fail feedback.

Call this when you've completed the work for a task with manual validation.
The task's module evaluates your work against its criteria.

On pass: the task is marked completed and the requirement is rechecked.
On fail: you receive feedback describing what needs fixing.

Tasks with automatic validation are evaluated by the stop hook — you don't
need to call this for those.

The `session_id` is injected automatically by the PreToolUse hook.

agent_id.description: Whose task to close. An agent we run carries it on the connection and omits this.

handoff_id.description: Report assigned artifact completion instead of evaluating; does not close the task or launch validation.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

verification.description: Observed artifact and parent-gitlink verification; never a QA verdict.

name: list_session_subagents
description:
List all registered sub-agents on the current session, filtered by
the configured TTL (Story 704 / Rule 3).

Returns each sub-agent's identity, when they registered, and their
assignment status — idle (no Task in this session carries their
agent_id) or the task they own (via Task.agent_id match).

TTL-expired registrations are filtered out (lazy prune from Rule 2);
callers see the same truth the engineer's session detail page renders.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

name: list_tasks
description:
List tasks — your own, or a named agent's.

Returns task status, agent assignment, component, and requirement
so the main agent can track subagent progress.

Pass `agent_id` to read that agent's queue instead of your own. Without it
this answers about the caller, which is what every agent means when it asks
what it is holding.

agent_id.description: Whose tasks to list. Omit for your own; name an agent to read its queue.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

status.description: Filter by status: active, completed, failed, cancelled (optional)

name: list_user_questions
description:
Your unanswered questions, oldest first, with their linked task IDs.

Recovers what you asked before a compaction, or lets you check whether a
question is still open before asking another. Internal callers see their
own durable agent's questions across restarts; external callers see their
session's. Answered questions are not listed -- `check_answer` hands back
a reply once it lands, and there is no expiry: an unanswered question
stays listed until it is.

name: register_session
description:
Register this conversation as a session on the server.

Every task tool hangs off a session, and normally the SessionStart hook
creates it — the agent never thinks about it. That hook posts to the harness
on localhost, so a server the harness is not reporting to has no session for
the conversation, and every task tool dead-ends on `No session_id available`
with nothing the agent can do about it.

Deliberately explicit rather than implicit. A tool that silently invents a
session on first use hides which server the work is being recorded against,
and that is exactly the thing worth being sure of when two of them are
reachable. The task tools name this one in their error instead.

session_id.description: This conversation's id — Claude Code exposes it as CLAUDE_SESSION_ID

name: show_in_panel
description:
Put something in front of the person watching, beside the conversation —
never the page, so it never costs them the transcript or composer.

Call it when you start on a story, instead of describing where to look. It
never interrupts: it applies at once on a screen with room, or waits
behind a tap on a narrow one. There is no screen argument and no "was this
seen" answer — the view resolves that, and neither is something you act on.

story_number.description: Which story, when view is "story". Ignored otherwise.

view.description: What the panel should show. "stories" for the project's list, "story" for one, "epics" for the project's epics.

name: start_analysis
description:
Start an analyzer run and return immediately.

Sources: `spex`, `exunit`, `credo`, `compiler`. Returns as soon as the run is
opened — it does not wait, and you should not wait for it.

`paths` scopes the run to specific files, the same way the PreToolUse hook's
own `mix test test/foo_test.exs` rewrite does. Scoped runs can never satisfy
freshness — they cover only what they name — so use this for a focused
validation, not as a substitute for the full sweep `ready_for_qa` reads.

An agent running inside our own BEAM is sent the result as a message when the
run lands, so the thing to do after calling this is stop. A Claude Code
session collects it on its next tool call instead.

paths.description: Scope the run to these paths (e.g. one test file), instead of the full suite. Empty runs everything. A scoped run is `:partial` and can never satisfy freshness on its own — it covers only what it names.

name: start_task
description:
Start working on a requirement.

Takes a requirement (`requirement_name` + `entity_type` + `entity_id`, or
`requirement_name` + `module_name`, as `get_next_requirement` offers it),
creates and activates a task on its owner in one step, and returns the work
prompt.

The owner is the agent on the connection when there is one, otherwise the
Claude Code session whose `session_id` the PreToolUse hook injects. `agent_id`
may also carry a sub-agent label, which owns tasks on the caller's session.

If the owner already holds an open task for this requirement, it returns
that task's prompt (resuming a blocked one whose blocker is resolved)
without creating a duplicate.

See knowledge/tools, "start_task".

agent_id.description: Your agent identifier — claims ownership of the task

entity_id.description: The entity that owns this requirement: a story's number, or a component's or project's id

entity_type.description: Entity type: component, story, or project

module_name.description: Component module name (alternative to entity_id for component requirements)

requirement_name.description: Name of the requirement (e.g., implementation_file, ready_for_qa)

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

story_number.description: A story's number — the same as entity_type `story` with entity_id set to it

name: tap_out
description:
Voluntary tap-out of continuous mode (Story 704 / Rule 5; consumer of
538/5124).

Writes a `PermissionRequest` the person sees in their notifications inbox,
keyed to the agent we run or to the Claude Code session that asked. Returns
immediately; the caller does not wait. On approve, continuous clears (or the
linked task is cancelled). On reject, it stays on.

session_id.description: Injected by hook — do not set manually

task_id.description: Task to block; omit for whole-agent continuous stop approval.

name: withdraw_question
description:
Take back your own pending question once it is moot, with the reason. The
task it blocked is released; resume it with start_task.

reason.description: Why it no longer needs an answer.
